questions.sec: AR Signs i-l (top of Book p64)
questions.q: A patient's aortic regurgitation murmur is best heard over the right sternal border rather than at Erb's point. According to Book p64, what does that suggest?
opts: That the regurgitation is due to aneurysmal dilation
questions.exp: Book p64 sign i: 'When the murmur is best heard over the right sternal border, it suggests that the regurgitation is due to aneurysmal dilation.' (Book p64)

questions.sec: AR Signs i-l (top of Book p64)
questions.q: Per Book p64, which additional systolic finding can be present with aortic regurgitation?
opts: A mid systolic ejection murmur best heard in the aortic area and transmitted to the carotids
A pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla
A mid diastolic rumble at the apex with an opening snap
A continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle
questions.exp: Book p64 sign j: 'A mid systolic ejection murmur can also be heard best in the aortic area and transmitted to the carotids'. (Book p64)

questions.sec: AR Signs i-l (top of Book p64)
questions.q: Book p64 names two eponymous murmurs as signs k and l of aortic regurgitation, without elaborating them: the ____ murmur and the ____ murmur.
questions.exp: Book p64 signs k–l: 'k. Austin Flint murmur-  l. Cole Cecil murmur-' — the note lists the eponyms only, with nothing after the dashes. (Book p64)

questions.q: In the AR investigation list on Book p64, the only sub-item elaborated is under Doppler Echo: color doppler is the ____ for ____.
questions.exp: Book p64 investigations: b. Doppler Echo — i. 'color doppler : most sensitive for mild cases'. (Book p64)

questions.q: Match the three CXR findings of AR on Book p64 to their sign — 1) Cardiomegaly 2) Aortic root dilation 3) Aortic valve calcification … A) Cor bovinum / bovine heart B) Prominent aortic knuckle C) Sus for concomitant AS
questions.exp: Book p64 CXR findings: i. cardiomegaly -> cor bovinum / bovine heart; ii. aortic root dilation -> prominent aortic knuckle; iii. Aortic valve calcification -> sus for concomitant AS. (Book p64)

questions.q: All of the following are listed investigations for AR on Book p64 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Book p64 AR investigations: a. ECG — LVH; b. Doppler Echo (color doppler most sensitive for mild cases); c. CXR (three findings); d. Cardiac cath. Holter/ambulatory BP monitoring is not listed. (Book p64)

questions.q: Match the AR management entries on Book p64 to their detail — 1) Baseline medical 2) Chronic + significant volume overload 3) Surgical treatment 4) Ideal time for surgery … A) As in MS (IE or syphilitic aortitis needs Rx) B) Requires a vasodilator (hydralazine, nifedipine, or ACE inhibitor) C) AVR D) After haemodynamic / echogenic evidence of LVdys but before significant symptoms
questions.exp: Book p64 AR management: a. as in MS (IE or syphilitic aortitis needs Rx); b. chronic + significant vol overload: requires vasodilator (hydralazine, nifedipine, or ACE inh); c. Sx: AVR; ideal time: after haemodynamic / echogenic evidence of LVdys but before significant symptoms. (Book p64)

questions.q: A patient with chronic aortic regurgitation is found to have active infective endocarditis. What does the Book p64 AR management line ('as in MS …') say must happen here?
opts: The MS-style medical regimen proceeds, but IE or syphilitic aortitis needs Rx
Vasodilators are withheld until the endocarditis is cured
Immediate AVR regardless of haemodynamic status
No medical therapy — surgical AVR alone
questions.exp: Book p64 management a: 'as in MS ( IE or syphilitic aortitis needs Rx )' — the parenthetical singles out IE and syphilitic aortitis as conditions that require treatment. (Book p64)

questions.q: For chronic AR with significant volume overload, Book p64 requires a vasodilator — listing ____, ____, or ____.
questions.exp: Book p64 management b: 'chronic + significant vol overload : requires vasodilator ( hydralazine , nifedipine , or ACE inh )'. (Book p64)

questions.q: In the ASD types on Book p64, ostium secundum ASD accounts for ____% and ostium primum ASD for ____%.
questions.exp: Book p64 ASD types: a. Ostium secundum ASD — 90%; b. Ostium primum ASD 5%. (Book p64)

questions.q: Ostium primum ASD on Book p64 is commonly associated with:
opts: Marfan syndrome or a bicuspid aortic valve
Down syndrome or endocardial cushion defects
Turner syndrome or coarctation of the aorta
Klinefelter syndrome or mitral valve prolapse
questions.exp: Book p64: 'Ostium primum ASD 5% — commonly associated with Down syndrome or endocardial cushion defects'. (Book p64)

questions.q: Match the five syndromic ASD associations on Book p64 to their listed detail — 1) Holt-Oram syndrome 2) Patau syndrome 3) Edward syndrome 4) Ellis van Creveld syndrome 5) Lutembacher syndrome … A) Triphalangeal (fingerised) thumb, sometimes abrachia or phocomelia B) Trisomy 13 C) Trisomy 18 D) Polydactyly, nail dysplasia, dwarfism E) MS + ASD
questions.exp: Book p64 syndromic associations: a. Holt-Oram (triphalangeal fingerised thumb, sometimes abrachia or phocomelia); b. Patau (trisomy 13); c. Edward (trisomy 18); d. Ellis van Creveld (polydactyly, nail dysplasia, dwarfism); e. Lutembacher — MS + ASD. (Book p64)

questions.q: Match the three Patau syndrome entries on Book p64 to their detail — 1) Chromosomal basis 2) Phenotype 3) Cardiac lesions … A) Trisomy 13 B) Polydactyly, flexion deformity of fingers, simian crease, cleft lip and palate, microcephaly C) ASD, VSD, PDA
questions.exp: Book p64 Patau syndrome: i. Trisomy 13; ii. Polydactyly, flexion deformity of fingers, simian crease, cleft lip and palate, microcephaly; iii. ASD, VSD, PDA. (Book p64)

questions.q: Match the three Edward syndrome entries on Book p64 to their detail — 1) Chromosomal basis 2) Phenotype 3) Cardiac lesions … A) Trisomy 18 B) Prominent occiput, low set malformed ears, rocker bottom feet, micrognathia, clenched fists C) ASD, VSD, PDA
questions.exp: Book p64 Edward syndrome: i. Trisomy 18; ii. Prominent occiput, low set malformed ears, rocker bottom feet, micrognathia, clenched fists; iii. ASD, VSD, PDA. (Book p64)

questions.q: All of the following are listed features of Edward syndrome on Book p64 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Edward syndrome (Book p64): prominent occiput, low set malformed ears, rocker bottom feet, micrognathia, clenched fists. Polydactyly belongs to Patau syndrome (and Ellis van Creveld), not Edward. (Book p64)

questions.q: All of the following are listed under the syndromic associations of ASD on Book p64 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The five listed syndromic associations (Book p64) are Holt-Oram, Patau, Edward, Ellis van Creveld and Lutembacher (MS + ASD). Williams syndrome is not listed here — the elfin-facies/hypercalcaemia phenotype appears on p61 beside supravalvular AS. (Book p64)

questions.q: The skeletal entry of Holt-Oram syndrome on Book p64: a triphalangeal (fingerised) thumb, sometimes ____ or ____.
questions.exp: Book p64 Holt-Oram syndrome: 'Triphalangeal (fingerised) thumb, sometimes abrachia or phocomelia'. (Book p64)

questions.q: The third and final point under ASD on Book p64 states:
opts: Atrial fibrillation is common in ASD
Complete heart block is common in ASD
Supraventricular tachycardia is common in ASD
Ventricular ectopy is common in ASD
questions.exp: Book p64, ASD point 3: 'Atrial fibrillation is common in ASD'. (Book p64)

units.title: AR Signs i–l — tail of the AR note (top of Book p64)
units.sec: AR Signs i-l (top of Book p64)
units.guide:
Right sternal border murmur -> aneurysmal dilation; a mid systolic ejection murmur can also be best in the aortic area, transmitted to the carotids.
Two eponymous murmurs are named without elaboration: Austin Flint and Cole Cecil.

units.title: AR Investigations (Book p64)
units.guide:
ECG — LVH; Doppler Echo (color doppler: most sensitive for mild cases); cardiac cath.
CXR: cardiomegaly (cor bovinum / bovine heart), aortic root dilation (prominent aortic knuckle), aortic valve calcification (sus for concomitant AS).

units.title: AR Management (Book p64)
units.guide:
As in MS (IE or syphilitic aortitis needs Rx); chronic + significant volume overload requires a vasodilator (hydralazine, nifedipine, or ACE inhibitor).
Surgery: AVR — ideal time after haemodynamic/echogenic evidence of LVdys but before significant symptoms.

units.title: Congenital HD — ASD: Types (Book p64)
units.guide:
Ostium secundum ASD = 90%; ostium primum ASD = 5%.
The primum type is commonly associated with Down syndrome or endocardial cushion defects.

units.title: Congenital HD — ASD: Syndromic Associations (Book p64)
units.guide:
Holt-Oram (triphalangeal fingerised thumb, sometimes abrachia or phocomelia); Patau — trisomy 13 (polydactyly, flexion deformity of fingers, simian crease, cleft lip and palate, microcephaly; ASD, VSD, PDA).
Edward — trisomy 18 (prominent occiput, low set malformed ears, rocker bottom feet, micrognathia, clenched fists; ASD, VSD, PDA); Ellis van Creveld (polydactyly, nail dysplasia, dwarfism); Lutembacher = MS + ASD.

units.title: Congenital HD — ASD: Atrial Fibrillation (Book p64)
units.guide:
The final point of the ASD section: atrial fibrillation is common in ASD.
This arrhythmic point closes the congenital heart disease page.
